calls.head: Ottawa gets to the dangerous areas
calls.body: Ottawa ranks 3rd of 32 for shot quality (one expected goal for every 14.8 unblocked shots); Detroit ranks 25th for keeping shots to the outside.
calls.call: Ottawa needs no more than its usual 14.8 unblocked shots per expected goal.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: Ottawa needed 19.0 unblocked shots per expected goal, against its usual 14.8.

calls.head: Airtight against leaky on the kill
calls.body: Ottawa ranks 2nd of 32 for penalty kill, toward the airtight end; Detroit ranks 21st, toward the leaky end.
calls.call: Ottawa’s penalty kill allows less per 60 than Detroit’s.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On expected goals allowed per 60 on the penalty kill, Ottawa had 12.0 per 60 and Detroit 6.3 per 60. Coming in, Ottawa was at 6.8 per 60 and Detroit at 7.9 per 60.

DET.head: We had this close to even (45% for Detroit), and Detroit came through.

OTT.head: We had this close to even (55% for Ottawa), and it went Detroit’s way.

surprises.head: Detroit brought the hits
surprises.body: Detroit’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 178, against its usual 97 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 60 games.

surprises.head: Detroit tried a different line
surprises.body: A. Copp, K. Kolesar, M. Rasmussen played 10:09 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Detroit’s usual lines.
